title: Numbers, Time & Money
tagline: Numbers, prices, telling the time, days and age.
canDo: You can handle prices, times, dates and your age

grammar.title: Numbers
grammar.body: 1–10: ek, do, teen, chaar, paanch, chhe, saat, aath, nau, das. Round numbers: bees (20), tees (30), chaalees (40), pachaas (50), sau (100), hazaar (1,000). 11–99 are each their own word; learn them as you need them.

grammar.title: Telling time
grammar.body: X baje = X o'clock. sawa X = X:15, saare X = X:30, paune X = (X−1):45. Two special halves: derh (1:30) and dhai (2:30).

grammar.title: kal
grammar.body: kal means both yesterday and tomorrow, and parson both the day before yesterday and the day after tomorrow. The verb's tense tells you which.

phrases.en: How much did you pay for it?
phrases.note: The desi national pastime. Ask anyone about anything they own.
saare = and a half. Saare teen = 3½ = 3:30.
paune = a quarter less than. Paune chaar = 3¾.
Same word. The verb tense tells you which. Yes, really.

phrases.en: the day after tomorrow (or before yesterday)

phrases.note: In desi time, this means 45 minutes. Plan accordingly.

phrases.roman: Yeh naye joote hain? Kitne ka liya?
phrases.urdu: یہ نئے جوتے ہیں؟ کتنے کا لیا؟
phrases.en: Are those new shoes? How much did you pay?
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Paanch hazaar?! Hamare zamane mein das rupay ke aate the!
phrases.urdu: پانچ ہزار؟! ہمارے زمانے میں دس روپے کے آتے تھے!
phrases.en: Five thousand?! In my day they cost ten rupees!
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Achha… Sasta? Phir mere liye bhi le aana
phrases.urdu: اچھا… سستا؟ پھر میرے لیے بھی لے آنا
phrases.en: Oh… cheap? Then get me a pair too
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Aur tumhari umar kya hai ab?
phrases.urdu: اور تمہاری عمر کیا ہے اب؟
phrases.en: And how old are you now?
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Nani, main pachees saal ka hoon
phrases.urdu: نانی، میں پچیس سال کا ہوں

phrases.roman: Pachees! Teri Ammi ki is umar mein shaadi ho gayi thi
phrases.urdu: پچیس! تیری امی کی اس عمر میں شادی ہو گئی تھی
phrases.en: Twenty-five! Your mum was married at your age
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Achha, aaj kitne baje wapas aaoge?
phrases.urdu: اچھا، آج کتنے بجے واپس آؤ گے؟
phrases.en: Right, what time will you be back today?
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Paanch minute… Tumhare paanch minute mujhe pata hain
phrases.urdu: پانچ منٹ… تمہارے پانچ منٹ مجھے پتا ہیں
phrases.en: Five minutes… I know your five minutes
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Yeh paanch sau rupay ka hai
phrases.urdu: یہ پانچ سو روپے کا ہے
phrases.en: This one is five hundred rupees
phrases.speaker: bashir

phrases.roman: Paanch sau? Bohat mehnga hai. Teen sau
phrases.urdu: پانچ سو؟ بہت مہنگا ہے۔ تین سو
phrases.en: Five hundred? Far too expensive. Three hundred
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Kal subah saat baje nikalna hai. Saat. Sawa saat nahin.
phrases.urdu: کل صبح سات بجے نکلنا ہے۔ سات۔ سوا سات نہیں۔
phrases.en: We leave at seven tomorrow morning. Seven. Not quarter past.
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: Agle din Abbu saadhe chhe baje gaari mein baithe the.
phrases.urdu: اگلے دن ابو ساڑھے چھ بجے گاڑی میں بیٹھے تھے۔
phrases.en: The next day Abbu was sitting in the car at half past six.

phrases.roman: Ammi saat baj kar bees minute par aayin.
phrases.urdu: امی سات بج کر بیس منٹ پر آئیں۔
phrases.en: Ammi came out at twenty past seven.

phrases.roman: Bees minute der! Kya kar rahi thin?
phrases.urdu: بیس منٹ دیر! کیا کر رہی تھیں؟
phrases.en: Twenty minutes late! What were you doing?
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: Aap ke liye parathe bana rahi thi.
phrases.urdu: آپ کے لیے پراٹھے بنا رہی تھی۔
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Abbu chup ho gaye aur chaar parathe kha gaye.
phrases.urdu: ابو چپ ہو گئے اور چار پراٹھے کھا گئے۔
phrases.en: Abbu went quiet and ate four parathas.

phrases.roman: Hum saadhe aath baje pahunche. Sab khush the.
phrases.urdu: ہم ساڑھے آٹھ بجے پہنچے۔ سب خوش تھے۔
phrases.en: We arrived at half past eight. Everyone was happy.

lessons.blurb: 1 to 10. The building blocks of every bargain.

teach.title: Counting
teach.info: Urdu numbers are old friends of Hindi ones: ek, do, teen… Learn 1–10 now; bigger numbers come next.

options.feedback: Not even close. It's a number.

lessons.title: Bees, pachaas, sau
lessons.blurb: The round numbers (and why 1–100 is a vocabulary list).
lessons.canDo: You can say round numbers up to a thousand

teach.title: Every number is its own word
teach.info: In Urdu, 21–99 are not 'twenty-one' built from parts. Each is its own word (ikkees, baees, teyees…). Native speakers often switch to English for big numbers. Start with the round ones.

exercises.prompt: Khala says the shalwar kameez cost “do hazaar”. How much?

lessons.title: Kitne ka hai?
lessons.blurb: Prices, gasping at prices, and asking everyone what they paid.
lessons.canDo: You can ask prices and react to them

teach.tip: Say it with feeling. Even if it isn't.

exercises.prompt: The shopkeeper names a price. Act shocked.
Your aunt sees your new phone. What's her first question?

lessons.title: Kitne baje?
lessons.blurb: Telling time the desi way: saare, sawa, paune.
lessons.canDo: You can tell and ask the time, including half and quarter past

teach.title: Special halves
teach.info: Two times have their own words: derh (1:30) and dhai (2:30). After that it's regular: saare teen, saare chaar…

lessons.title: Aaj, kal, parson
lessons.blurb: Days, ages, and the five-minute lie.
lessons.canDo: You can talk about when things happen and say your age

teach.tip: Kal = yesterday AND tomorrow. Context does the rest.

exercises.prompt: “Main kal aaunga” (I will come). Kal means…

options.feedback: The verb is future (aaunga), so it's tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Say you're 20: “My age is twenty years”
Your cousin says “Bas paanch minute mein!” When will they arrive?

lessons.title: Mix it up
lessons.blurb: Nani has seen your new shoes. Warm up for the boss.
lessons.canDo: You can use this unit's phrases without a prompt: you can handle prices, times, dates and your age

teach.title: Nani has seen your new shoes
teach.info: She's about to ask what they cost, how old you are and when you'll be home. Have your numbers ready.

exercises.setup: Bashir Bhai's shop. Ammi has picked up a dupatta.
exercises.question: What price does Ammi offer?

options.feedback: That's Bashir Bhai's price. She says teen sau.

exercises.prompt: Type it for the family group: “What time is it?”

boss.title: Nani's Price Check
boss.blurb: Nani spots your new shoes. Then asks your age. Then your curfew. Numbers under pressure.
boss.scene: You're putting on new shoes by the front door when you feel a presence behind you. Nani has seen the shoes. Nani has questions.
boss.canDo: You can answer questions about prices, your age and times without panicking

b.prompt: Tell her the price. Or lie.

e.prompt: Tell her your age. (She knows. She was there.)

options.reaction: Answering an elder's question with sass. She lets it go, because she's about to win.
You used the five-minute lie on the woman who invented it.

end.title: Price check passed
end.text: Prices, ages, times: all answered in Urdu, under Nani's gaze. You're home by ten. (You're home by eleven.)

story.title: Seven o'clock sharp
story.blurb: Abbu said seven. He meant it. Ammi had other plans.

questions.question: What time did Abbu want to leave?

options.feedback: Sawa saat nahin: NOT quarter past.
That's when he got in the car. Early, as always.

options.text: She was making parathas for Abbu

options.feedback: She was cooking: parathe bana rahi thi.
She was up before him, cooking.
